findings.element: .b-item / .b-grab rows on owner-flight, and the four .b-step buttons inside .b-edit
findings.problem: Driven at 1440: document.querySelectorAll('[draggable]') is 0, there is not one pointerdown/mousedown/dragstart binding in the document, no element computes a grab or move cursor, and with a row focused ArrowUp/ArrowDown/ArrowLeft/ArrowRight do nothing but scroll the page (focus never moves; Home leaves the focused row at y=967, off screen). The thesis of this instrument is that position IS the quantity — the whole scale argument, 14/18/12/8/2 pixels a day, rests on it — yet the quantity is untouchable. Moving a moment costs: hover the row to learn 'Edit' is a control, click, wait for the docked panel, then find one of four 44x40 stepper buttons or retype a date. The class is literally named b-grab and it does not grab. Linear, Things and Notion all let you take hold of the thing whose position is the point; this surface asks you to describe the move to a form instead of making it. Everything else in the interaction model is strong, which is exactly why this reads as the missing verb rather than a missing feature.
findings.fix: Give the rail a pointer grab and a keyboard equivalent, both writing through the same move accessor the steppers already use so undo, the readout, the count, the gap note and the announcement all keep working unchanged. Pointer: on .b-grab pointerdown, set cursor:grabbing, set data-lifted="true" on the .b-item (the fore-06 tint the editing state already uses, plus the 12px halo), track pointermove against the same pixels-per-day constant the render uses, snap to whole days, and commit on pointerup by calling move(item, deltaDays); Escape during the drag cancels and returns the row to its origin pixel. Keyboard: with a .b-grab focused, ArrowUp/ArrowDown move the moment one day earlier/later and Shift+Arrow one week, preventDefault so the page does not scroll, scrollIntoView({block:'nearest'}) after each commit so the moved row stays on screen, and announce through the same live region the stepper readout uses. Extend the row's accessible name to end 'Arrow keys move it a day, Shift and arrow a week' so the model is advertised where it is available. Both paths must honour the two ceilings that already exist (nothing past the day itself, nothing outside the measure) and both must push onto the existing undo stack.

findings.element: The owner action row (.b-act: Add a moment 123x39, Preview 79x39, Publish 75x39), the editor (.b-step 44x40 with 10px gaps, .b-seg Shown 70x37 / Hidden 72x37, Done 61x39, Delete this moment 145x39) and owner-empty (Set the day 102x39), all measured at 390x844
findings.problem: The audit gate's hit-target floor is 28px, so every one of these passes automation. But the master itself writes the real floor down, in its own comment on .b-behindSummary: '44px is the floor for a thing a thumb presses.' It then applies 44 to the one control a guest gets and to nothing the owner touches. On a 390px screen every owner control is 37-40px tall, and the four steppers — the most-pressed control on the surface, since stepping is currently the only way to change the one quantity the product is about — sit 44px wide with 10px between them, so 'a week earlier' and 'a day earlier' are 54px apart centre to centre. A planner standing in a venue moving a fitting will mis-tap. The undo is good enough that a mis-tap is recoverable, which is the only reason this is a 0.4 and not more.
findings.fix: Add a coarse-pointer block: @media (pointer: coarse) { .b-act, .b-seg button, .b-step { min-height: 44px } .b-step { min-width: 52px } .b-editActs, .b-stepRow { gap: 14px } }. Keep the visual box where it is at fine pointer so the 1440 composition is untouched. For the steppers specifically, do not just grow the boxes — separate the two magnitudes: put the two day steps adjacent and set the two week steps off by var(--gap-snug), so the pair a mis-tap costs most is not the pair sitting closest together.

findings.problem: Measured. At rest: border-color rgba(0,0,0,0), colour fore-72, padding-left 0px — drawn exactly like the inert text this lab deliberately uses to mean 'not built'. On hover it gains a fore-46 border, full ink, and 12px of left padding: the box goes 144.6px to 156.6px and the words 'Delete this moment' jump 12px to the right at the instant the pointer arrives. transition-property is 'border-color, background-color', so the padding is not in it — the label does not slide, it snaps out from under the cursor. Then the keyboard: focused with the pointer parked at 0,0, computed padding-left is 0px, border-color is transparent, colour is still 0.72. The rule is :hover only. So the one control on the surface that destroys a moment from a wedding plan is the one whose affordance a keyboard user never sees — and the tab order puts it last, one Tab past 'Done', which is the natural 'I have finished' keystroke. One Tab and one Enter from finishing is a deletion, on a control that to that user still looks like a caption.
findings.fix: Reserve the indent at rest and let ink alone carry the state, and add focus-visible to the same rule: .b-editDanger .b-act { border-color: transparent; color: var(--fore-72); padding-left: var(--gap-snug); } .b-editDanger .b-act:hover, .b-editDanger .b-act:focus-visible { border-color: var(--fore-46); color: var(--fore); }. Nothing reflows, and the keyboard user sees the control arm exactly as the pointer user does. Leave the DOM order as it is — the rule and the separate line are the right decision — but extend the accessible name to 'Delete this moment. Send the invitations' so the thing being destroyed is spoken before the key is pressed, matching the pattern the on-screen label already follows.

findings.element: .b-edit docked panel and the .b-item list, owner-flight to owner-editing
findings.problem: Driven: Enter on the third row opens the editor and focus lands on the panel (correct, and the panel names the moment). Eleven Tabs walk the panel cleanly. The twelfth press — past the last control — lands on 'Edit Menu tasting at The Orchard', the FIRST row in the list, then the second, and only on the fourteenth press do you reach the row you were actually editing. The panel is docked in the left column and therefore precedes the whole list in DOM order, so leaving it forward throws you to the top of the plan. Escape is handled and proven; forward Tab is the other half of the same journey and nobody designed it. A planner editing the fifth of seven moments and tabbing onward has to cross four rows to get back to where they were looking.
findings.fix: On the panel's last focusable control, handle keydown for Tab without shiftKey: preventDefault, then focus the .b-grab of the item carrying data-editing="true" and scrollIntoView({block:'nearest'}). Mirror it on the panel container for Shift+Tab from the first control. This keeps the docked, non-trapping model exactly as decided — nothing is captured, both edges simply hand focus back to the row the panel is about, which is where the reader's eye already is.

findings.problem: The frame marks itself aria-busy, invents no measure, shimmers at nothing and says 'Bringing in what is ahead' — all of which the gate proves and all of which is right. What it also has, measured, is exactly zero focusable elements. There is no retry, no link, no control of any kind. That is correct for the first second and wrong for the tenth: if the fetch stalls on a phone in a venue with two bars of signal, the guest holds a screen that says something is coming, forever, with nothing to press and nothing to read. The 'ended' state proves this team knows how to write a dead-end honestly — a stalled load is the same class of moment and has no designed frame at all. This is the undesigned edge, in the one state a guest is most likely to hit on the morning itself.
findings.fix: Give the loading node a second frame on the same element after 8 seconds: drop aria-busy to false, replace the line with 'This is taking longer than it should. The plan is still there.' and render one .b-act 'Try again' as the only control, focused. Keep the reserved geometry and the promised name exactly as they are so nothing hops between the two frames — the same discipline the first frame already keeps against the data landing. Add it to the state matrix as state=loading-slow so it is shot and gated like every other state.

biggestWin: The single thing holding this seat below 9.5 is that position — the one quantity this whole instrument exists to express — cannot be touched: there is no drag on the rail and no arrow-key move on a focused row, so the most frequent owner action is buried two levels down in a docked form, and until a moment can be taken hold of and moved directly, the interaction model is describing the timeline rather than being one.
